summary: @servicetitan/anvil-fonts preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated sibling payload
details: This font-distribution package declares a preinstall lifecycle hook `node setup.mjs`. `setup.mjs` is itself obfuscated (hex-random identifiers, string-map dispatchers) and probes for a system `bun` binary; when absent, it downloads a Bun runtime from oven-sh's GitHub releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it 0755, and uses that fresh Bun binary to execute the sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync(bunPath, [join(D,'math_init.js')], {stdio:'inherit', cwd:D})`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with a large numeric string-map (`n7gIxM`), a rotation function (`WV8StW`), and a custom-alphabet decoder (`hc1jfK9`); all identifiers are hex-random and endpoints/strings are reassembled at runtime from the map rather than appearing as literals. The README advertises this package as a static font/CSS/SCSS/LESS asset bundle consumed by webpack — only `dist/` needs to ship — so a preinstall hook that fetches a second language runtime and executes an obfuscated ~727KB bundle under it has no relationship to the package's stated purpose. Executing the payload under a freshly dropped Bun runtime also bypasses tooling that only inspects Node-resolved code paths. Behavior is consistent with a hijacked or typosquatted release of this scope's font package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
